node-1.label: Wart-like lesions developed on the patient's face 2 weeks after facial rejuvenation procedure

node-2.label: A white woman in her 60s presented for facial rejuvenation with panfacial lipoatrophy and photodamaged skin, and a medical history of nasal basal cell carcinoma.

node-3.label: She underwent fractional CO2 laser resurfacing and fat transfer to her temples, forehead, and midface.

node-4.label: Physical examination revealed firm, verrucoid keratotic papules on the face that were itchy and irritated.

node-5.label: The lesions did not respond to conservative treatment including hydrocortisone, mupirocin ointment, and topical crisaborole ointment.

why.why: Two biopsies showed verrucous actinic keratosis with atypical squamous proliferation and no koilocytes or viral cytopathic effect. Expert pathology and laboratory analyses interpret these findings as not supporting HPV viral wart. HPV PCR/genotyping was not obtained, so viral etiology cannot be completely excluded, but the histologic evidence markedly reduces the likelihood of post-laser HPV wart. Confidence lowered from 0.35 to 0.10.

Histologic examination revealed verrucous actinic keratosis with atypical squamous proliferation rather than a benign keratosis. This precancerous pattern, supported by both expert analyses, makes benign keratotic papules very unlikely. Confidence lowered from 0.20 to 0.05.

Two biopsies showed verrucous actinic keratosis with atypical squamous proliferation and no koilocytes or viral cytopathic effect. Expert pathology analysis strongly supports a precancerous/neoplastic process rather than viral wart or benign keratotic papules, and the patient's photodamage and prior basal cell carcinoma further align. Lack of response to conservative therapy also argues against dermatitis. HPV PCR/genotyping was not obtained, so viral etiology cannot be completely excluded, but the available evidence strongly favors skin cancer/precancer; confidence raised from 0.80 to 0.90.

Although the procedure can induce skin inflammation, the lesions did not respond to topical steroids/antibiotics/anti-inflammatory therapy, and two biopsies demonstrated verrucous actinic keratosis with atypical squamous proliferation rather than dermatitis. Expert pathology analysis also concludes that unresponsiveness argues against dermatitis, so confidence is lowered from 0.10 to 0.05.

node-12.label: Patient has verrucous actinic keratosis (precancerous keratosis)

why.why: The verrucoid keratotic papules, failure of conservative therapy, and two biopsies demonstrating verrucous actinic keratosis with atypical squamous proliferation and no koilocytes or viral cytopathic effect strongly support this specific precancerous diagnosis. Expert pathology analysis explicitly favors verrucous actinic keratosis and refutes viral wart and benign keratotic papules; the patient's photodamage and prior basal cell carcinoma are additional supporting factors. HPV PCR/genotyping was not performed, so viral etiology cannot be entirely excluded, which keeps confidence at 0.85 rather than higher.
